correctness.rationale: Condition on X, so P(X/Y>z|X)=min(1,(X/z)^q), and put a=theta/z^2, s=q/2. Since theta/X^2 is unit exponential, the exact tail is 1−exp(−a)+a^s Gamma(1−s,a), with Gamma(1−s,a)=∫_a^∞ exp(−t)t^(−s)dt. Differentiating this exact expression, not an asymptotic equivalent, gives f(z)=q a^s Gamma(1−s,a)/z; the moving-limit terms cancel. The integral tends to Gamma(1−s) for s<1, grows as log(1/a) for s=1, and is equivalent to a^(1−s)/(s−1) for s>1. In the last case the 1−exp(−a) term also contributes at order a, giving s/(s−1), not 1/(s−1), for the survival constant. Division of the exact leading terms gives z h(z)→min(q,2). For every real r>0, Tonelli and independence factor E[Z^r] as theta^(r/2) times ∫_0^∞ t^(−r/2)e^(−t)dt times ∫_0^1 q y^(q−r−1)dy. The two integrals have strict cutoffs r<2 and r<q, respectively, and their finite values are Gamma(1−r/2) and q/(q−r), as claimed. There is no finite variance; when q≤1 the mean itself is not finite. The mathematical conclusions hold; the wording at RESULT.md line 236 about differentiating regular variation is not valid in general, but the cited exact density justifies this step here. The uploaded numerical checker was inspected, not executed and is not used as proof.

evidence: Breiman's theorem yields both off-critical survival constants: for q<2 multiply the Pareto tail by E[X^q], and for q>2 multiply the inverse-Rayleigh tail by E[Y^(−2)]. At equality the needed extra moment fails. Rivera et al. treat a Rayleigh-parent slash law with all parent positive moments, so their cutoff r<q does not itself cover the inverse-Rayleigh cutoff.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Breiman alone does not prove the critical logarithm. The exact same-model formulas and the existing E_s expansions, not an extension of Breiman under failed hypotheses, settle that case.

evidence: For s=1, exact S=1−e^(−a)+a E_1(a) gives S~a ln(1/a), and exact f=(q/z)a E_1(a) gives the matching density constant. For s>1, S~a[1+1/(s−1)]; for s<1 the E_s term dominates 1−e^(−a). Divide to obtain the stated hazard. Proposition 8 states regular variation, not an incorrect explicit value of the index; the checked proof passage leaves calculation of the final ratio implicit. Proposition 6 gives the mean, and the all-real moments follow directly from (2.1) by the exponential and beta power integrals.

value.rationale: The tail index and the distinction between an exact power and a logarithmically modified power matter for extreme-value work. As a standalone finding, however, this fixed-q list is obtained by reading the leading term from a standard table for the exact function already in the model, and the moment and hazard assertions require only factorization and division. The source already correctly states regular variation; there is no contradicted index theorem being corrected. The record neither addresses the moving-parameter crossover nor derives another nonroutine consequence.
